fact_text: The EU Blue Card is a special residence permit under Section 18g of the Residence Act (AufenthG) for skilled workers who hold a higher education qualification or a higher-level training course of at least three years.
evidence_quote: The EU Blue Card (§ 18g AufenthG) is a special residence permit for skilled workers who hold a higher education qualification or who have completed a higher-level training course which lasted at least three years.

fact_text: The first Skilled Immigration Act entered into force in March 2020; the further reform (Law on the further development of skilled worker immigration) has been implemented since November 2023, expanding third-country entry options for jobseeking, employment and qualification recognition.
evidence_quote: The first Skilled Immigration Act, which entered into force in March 2020, started to facilitate the immigration of skilled workers from third countries. Implementation of the “Law on the further development of skilled worker immigration” has been ongoing since November 2023.

fact_text: For a non-regulated occupation, entry for employment can be possible WITHOUT formal recognition of the foreign qualification where the applicant has at least two years of relevant professional experience plus a specific job offer, a minimum salary and a qualified qualification; the Central Office for Foreign Education (ZAB) checks the qualification.
evidence_quote: This applies, for example, to persons who have at least two years of relevant, professional practical experience . The requirements in this case include a specific job offer, a certain minimum salary, and a qualified vocational or higher education qualification. The Central Office for Foreign Education (ZAB) checks whether someone has such a qualification.

fact_text: IT specialists may enter Germany to work even without a completed vocational or higher education qualification, provided they have the necessary professional experience and a job offer (and are employed in a non-regulated occupation).
evidence_quote: IT specialists may enter Germany in order to work even if they have not completed a vocational or higher education qualification as long as they have the necessary professional experience and have a job offer.

fact_text: The job search opportunity card (Chancenkarte) is a residence option under Section 20a of the Residence Act (AufenthG).
evidence_quote: The job search opportunity card (§ 20a AufenthG)

fact_text: As a rule third-country nationals require a residence permit; the Residence Act provides for Visas, Temporary residence permits, EU Blue Cards, ICT Cards, Mobile ICT Cards, Permanent settlement permits and EU long-term residence permits.
evidence_quote: As a rule, third-country nationals require some type of residence permit. The Residence Act provides for the following types of residence permits: Visas Temporary residence permits EU Blue Cards ICT Cards Mobile ICT Cards Permanent settlement permits EU long-term residence permits

fact_text: The EU Blue Card is the most important residence permit for academically trained skilled workers; it gives eligibility for a permanent settlement permit after fewer years of lawful residence, easier family reunification, and holders may leave Germany for up to 12 months without the card expiring.
evidence_quote: The EU Blue Card is the most important residence permit for skilled workers with academic training. It offers certain advantages, such as eligibility for a permanent settlement permit after fewer years of lawful residencefewer requirements for the subsequent immigration of family members And holders of an EU Blue Card may leave Germany for up to 12 months without the card expiring; most other types of residence permit expire if the holder remains outside of the country for more than six months.

fact_text: Anyone who moves into a dwelling must register with the registration authority (Meldebehörde) within two weeks of moving in — the statutory Anmeldung requirement under Section 17(1) of the Federal Registration Act (Bundesmeldegesetz).
evidence_quote: Wer eine Wohnung bezieht, hat sich innerhalb von zwei Wochen nach dem Einzug bei der Meldebehörde anzumelden.

fact_text: Visas are issued by the Federal Foreign Office's diplomatic missions abroad; all other residence permits (e.g. the EU Blue Card / Aufenthaltserlaubnis) are issued by the foreigners authorities (Ausländerbehörde) inside Germany after arrival.
evidence_quote: The Federal Foreign Office’s diplomatic representations abroad issue visas. All other types of residence permits are issued by the foreigners authorities in Germany.

fact_text: Residence permits are issued as a plastic card in credit-card format containing a computer chip storing the holder's personal information and biometric data (photograph and fingerprints).
evidence_quote: Residence permits are issued in the form of a plastic card in credit-card format. Inside the card is a computer chip on which the holder’s personal information (name, date of birth, nationality, address) and biometric data (photograph and fingerprints) are stored, along with any restrictions that apply to the holder.

fact_text: Permanent settlement permits and EU long-term residence permits have no expiry date; all other residence permits are issued for a limited period and may be extended only if the holder still meets the original requirements.
evidence_quote: Permanent settlement permits and EU long-term residence permits do not have a date of expiry. The other types of residence permits are issued for a limited period of time. They may be extended if the holder still meets the requirements that applied when the permit was initially issued.

fact_text: The German tax identification number (IdNo / Steueridentifikationsnummer) is an eleven-digit number that is permanently valid and does not change if you move house, change your name or change your marital status.
evidence_quote: The identification number (IdNo) concerns an eleven-digit number, and does not contain any information about the person concerned. It is permanently valid and does not change, for example, if you move house, change your name or change your marital status.

fact_text: The IdNo is assigned to uniquely identify a natural person in administrative proceedings; the number and stored data are subject to purpose limitation under Section 139b of the German Fiscal Code (AO).
evidence_quote: This identification number is assigned for the purpose of uniquely identifying a natural person in administrative proceedings. For example, the identification number enables the tax administration to provide services, such as a pre-filled tax return form provided on an electronic basis, or the automated processing of electronic receipts. The use of this and any data stored to this end are subject to purpose limitation in accordance with Section 139b of the German Fiscal Code (AO).

fact_text: For data-protection reasons the IdNo can only be communicated by post; a new arrival who has not received it can request it via the BZSt input form or by letter, and it usually also appears on the income tax assessment or the employment tax statement.
evidence_quote: Please understand that the IdNo can only be communicated to you through the mail for data protection reasons.

fact_text: To provide employers with automatically retrievable wage-tax deduction data (ELStAM), the BZSt stores additional reporting data for each taxpayer under Section 39e(2) of the Income Tax Act (EStG), including religious affiliation and marital status — the basis for church tax and tax class in payroll withholding.
evidence_quote: For the purpose of providing employers with automatically retrievable wage tax deduction data, the BZSt also stores additional reporting data for each taxpayer in accordance with Section 39e (2) of the Income Tax Act (EStG). This concerns reporting data: pertaining to religious affiliationpertaining to a person’s marital status under registration law

fact_text: Germany has signed mutual social security agreements with 20 countries; the agreement with India applies from 1 May 2017 (date signed / in force listed as 1.5.2017).
evidence_quote: The Federal Republic of Germany has currently signed mutual social security agreements with 20 countries.

fact_text: The German social security agreements (including the one with India) essentially regulate the acquisition of pension eligibility and the payment of pensions in the respective countries.
evidence_quote: These agreements essentially regulate the acquisition of pension eligibility and the payment of pensions in the respective countries.

fact_text: The social security agreement primarily benefits the nationals of the respective agreement countries (so it applies to Indian nationals moving to Germany), though depending on the agreement it can extend to other persons.
evidence_quote: The social security agreement primarily benefits the nationals of the respective agreement countries.

fact_text: Each insurance agency checks pension entitlement individually under its own national law and pays its own pension; there is no single European or overall pension paid by one country on behalf of the others (contribution periods can be added up but pensions are separate).
evidence_quote: Each insurance agency checks individually whether there is a pension entitlement according to its national legal provisions and, if so, pays its pension. It is therefore possible that you may receive a pension from several countries, depending on where you have accrued periods of insurance and whether the eligibility requirements are fulfilled in each case. There is no “European pension” or “overall pension” that one member state and/or agreement country pays on behalf of the others.

fact_text: European coordination law (Regulation (EC) No 883/2004 and No 987/2009) can, under certain conditions, also apply to people who do not hold the nationality of a member state (third-country nationals).
evidence_quote: Furthermore European law can also apply under certain conditions to people who do not have the nationality of a member state (so-called third country nationals).

fact_text: Workers and employees employed for remuneration are subject to compulsory statutory health insurance (gesetzliche Krankenversicherung) under Section 5(1) No.1 of the Social Code Book V (SGB V).
evidence_quote: Versicherungspflichtig sind 1.Arbeiter, Angestellte und zu ihrer Berufsausbildung Beschäftigte, die gegen Arbeitsentgelt beschäftigt sind,

fact_text: Under family insurance (Familienversicherung, Section 10 SGB V) a member's spouse/partner and children resident in Germany are co-insured at no additional contribution, provided they are not otherwise insured and their total income does not regularly exceed one-seventh of the monthly reference figure.
evidence_quote: Versichert sind der Ehegatte, der Lebenspartner und die Kinder von Mitgliedern sowie die Kinder von familienversicherten Kindern, wenn diese Familienangehörigen 1.ihren Wohnsitz oder gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt im Inland haben

fact_text: Children are co-insured under family insurance up to age 18, up to age 23 if not gainfully employed, and up to age 25 if in school or vocational training.
evidence_quote: Kinder sind versichert 1.bis zur Vollendung des achtzehnten Lebensjahres,2.bis zur Vollendung des dreiundzwanzigsten Lebensjahres, wenn sie nicht erwerbstätig sind,3.bis zur Vollendung des fünfundzwanzigsten Lebensjahres, wenn sie sich in Schul- oder Berufsausbildung befinden

fact_text: Where family-insurance requirements are met with more than one fund, the member chooses the health insurance fund (Krankenkasse), reflecting the free choice of Krankenkasse in the statutory system.
evidence_quote: Sind die Voraussetzungen der Absätze 1 bis 4 mehrfach erfüllt, wählt das Mitglied die Krankenkasse.
